changes.old: Eligible authors, each supporting every governing proposition in full: Stone-Zsela, Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer. Minimum eligible count: 3. Ginsburg supplies the precise old-prosecution accommodation on which her and Kennedy's full joins depend: consider whether a further opportunity is proper without eliminating the patentee burden or requiring automatic reopening. changes.new:
Eligible authors, each supporting every governing proposition in full: Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer. Stone's express intent reservation makes him ineligible to deliver this entire opinion; his judgment membership still makes him the assigner. Minimum eligible count: 3. Balance pool: Stevens, Scalia, Kennedy, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer. The Chief assigns Ginsburg. She supplies the precise old-prosecution accommodation on which her and Kennedy's full joins depend: consider whether a further opportunity is proper without eliminating the patentee burden or requiring automatic reopening. Her authorship offers a concrete advantage in stating that qualification faithfully with the enforceable claim boundary. Breyer, at count 3, is the strongest eligible alternative because his frozen practical reservation also supports fair consideration of an old prosecution record. Ginsburg's recorded objection defines the exact accommodation and supports the rebuttable expansion preference within the pool despite her one additional prior lead. Stone can carry the other propositions but cannot be compared as an eligible whole-opinion author by disregarding his reservation. The opinion is not divided because eight eligible authors can carry the whole.

Current-Run final validation corrected the earlier draft's attribution of the intent proposition to Stone. Recounting the same actual preceding opinion tables gives the unchanged counts above, and Ginsburg remains within the corrected eligible pool. Her assignment, delivered scope and credit remain unchanged; no author lost the necessary coalition and no reassignment is made. The eight Associates' frozen commitments, their controlling intent rule and every judgment vote remain unchanged. This correction requires no new non-Stone commitment or historical-reconciliation ground. The [validation receipt](../freeze/OT_1996CHUNK5_WARNER_JOIN_VALIDATION.json) identifies the draft and final hashes; no prior completed Record is altered.

changes.old: Justice Ginsburg's Opinion of the Court is joined in full by the other eight participating Justices. All three holdings below, including the contextual treatment of older prosecution records, command nine votes.
changes.new: Justice Ginsburg's Opinion of the Court is joined in full by Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas and Breyer. Stone-Zsela joins all propositions except the statement that bad intent is not an element, which therefore has eight direct joins; he reserves that issue. Every other proposition below, including the contextual treatment of older prosecution records, has nine direct joins.

Chief Justice Stone-Zsela concurs in part and in the judgment. He joins the Court's opinion except its statement that bad intent is not an element of infringement under the doctrine of equivalents. He reserves intent-based infringement and supports the element-specific remand and the patentee's explanatory burden without deciding that issue. No other Justice joins this reservation.
